en: The Philippine flag features a sun with 8 rays, representing the first 8 provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule in 1896.
Spain sold the Philippines to the United States for 20 million dollars in 1898, ending 333 years of Spanish colonial rule.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of a Senate with exactly 24 elected members and a House of Representatives with over 300 members.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct living languages, but Filipino and English are the 2 official languages used in government and education.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces, which stand approximately 1,500 meters above sea level and were carved 2,000 years ago.
The Tamaraw, the national animal of the Philippines, stands only about 1 meter tall at the shoulder and weighs up to 300 kilograms.
National hero Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed by firing squad on December 30, 1896.
The annual Sinulog festival in Cebu City attracts over 2 million visitors to celebrate the Santo Niño every third Sunday of January.
Filipino citizens must be at least 18 years old to vote in national elections, which are held regularly every 3 years.
Dr. Fe del Mundo founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines in 1957, dedicating over 70 years to pediatric medicine.
The Philippines is divided into 17 administrative regions, including the National Capital Region, which contains exactly 16 cities and 1 municipality.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution contains 18 articles, with Article III specifically detailing the Bill of Rights across 22 distinct sections.
